- If sentiment is positive (≥ 0.10) in recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast slightly.
- If sentiment is negative (≤ -0.10) in recent days, model tends to underestimate; increase forecast slightly.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3-5 days), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above recent peak.
- If model shows steady upward trend with no recent volatility, true price often reverses or flattens; reduce slope or add downward buffer.
- If true outcome shows early sharp drop after forecast peak, model may be lagging; adjust forecast to reflect recent sentiment reversal.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overfits recent trend; apply mean reversion if sentiment is neutral or weak (0.00–0.05).
- If sentiment history shows alternating +/– swings, model may misread momentum; use sentiment-weighted average of recent 5–7 days for correction.
